summary: ITEM 1: THE TWO SITES THAT ARE MINE WERE ALREADY APPLIED AT HEAD AND I VERIFIED BOTH RATHER THAN RE-APPLYING THEM -- docs/04_CONTRACT.md's CAP parenthetical now reads '(`spine/lever.py::Lever` carries `choices` and, since 2026-09-14, an optional `domain=(lo, hi)` -- CAP declares one on neither lever)', which I confirmed by AST (src/capacity/levers.py declares 0 domains), and the quotation of src/lm/api.py::resolve is left verbatim with the first clause marked out of date and the requote filed against lm's owner, which is the right handling because O13 checks the quotation against the cited symbol. OF THE OTHER TWELVE FILED EDITS, FOUR ARE ALREADY DONE IN THE TREE and the report's anchors for them no longer match: src/sig/levers.py (both), src/opt/levers.py and src/opt/api.py, whose raised message no longer exists at all -- its sentence now sits in src/opt/levers.py in the PAST tense ('was once the only thing standing there'). EIGHT SURVIVE, all re-verified to resolve exactly once against the current tree, and TWO OF THE EIGHT NOW CARRY A FILED REPLACEMENT THAT IS ITSELF FALSE: both src/sig/api.py sites are inside warm_up and are about SIG_WARMUP_MIN_FRAC, which now DOES declare domain=(0.0, 1.0), so the filed text 'an optional domain= this lever does not declare' would replace one false sentence with another. Corrected text supplied for both, and flagged as COUPLED to the O15 ruling on that lever, because what is true there depends on which arm is taken. A NINTH DEFECT FOUND WHILE RE-VERIFYING, NOT IN THE REPORT: src/capacity/api.py::new_valve attributes to src/sig/levers.py::SIGLevers a sentence SIGLevers no longer contains, and O13 cannot see it because its quotation arm skips spans carrying code punctuation and this span carries '::'. That is the same false-quotation defect the same function already records having made once before against src/lm/api.py::resolve. ALL THREE STANDING U.FRACTION RULINGS WERE READ BEFORE ANY REWRITE and every correction states the range facility exists while keeping the unit a LABEL; nothing I wrote makes 'a fraction means 0..1' true by implication, and the doc's own item 2 of 'three things a reader must not infer' is unchanged. ITEM 2: D18 WRITTEN, carrying the evidence rather than the verdict -- the question was where the upper end LIVES and whether 'no ceiling' is typed or true by default; hi=None admits +inf (measured) and 163 of 207 get no ceiling, so domain= alone would have left +inf legal on 53 float levers, which is why the floor and the pair are complements; the limit is in the ruling itself at twenty-four orders of magnitude, with OPT_LR=1e6 destroying the model while finite and FAB_ALPHA=1e26 printing an ordinary loss over 15 of 23 poisoned gradient tensors; 131 have no derivable ceiling, 16 one the tree has explicitly declined, 15 one that is another lever and cannot be a pair at all; only 33 of 207 were populated and NOT ONE of the seven levers the sweep filed as critical for a magnitude is among them, said plainly; the floor's switch and what off costs; and the 1093-site / 78-file scan behind REFUSE_INEXACT_INT, which I re-ran independently under a narrower pattern (520 sites, 54 files) and which agrees exactly on the answer -- every non-exact hit in the tree is PROSE describing the defect, zero live configurations break. D18 also records what the ruling COST on the day: it MADE six untrippable guards, four since retired, two open. ITEM 3: THE BRIEF'S PREMISE FOR K1 IS REFUTED AND I PROVED IT RATHER THAN QUOTING THE TEST'S COMMENT -- K1's population is 132 entry points over the thirteen packages in PKG_DIR, spine is not among them, so a new Lever declaration field cannot reach K1 in either direction and no suite was waiting to fail. What the document owes is PROSE, and I found two live falsehoods in it, both mine: section 0.5's 'RED with six findings in four packages' and its 'F4 is red for the same reason' were both overtaken by the sibling fixes, and its parenthetical hedge that the published high-end breakdown 'does not sum to its own total' is simply wrong -- 44+16+15+131+1 = 207 and 16+15+131+1 = 163, and the low-end breakdown sums too, so the figures are now quoted instead of being described. tools/sync_counts.py --check and tools/render_wiring.py --check were both already current before and after my edits; there was no diff to read and nothing to act on. WHAT I DID NOT DO: I did not narrow, weaken or touch O15. It is still red, still reporting a true fact about two levers in two packages I do not own, and the document now names both of them.

The claim 'CAP declares one on neither lever' is TRUE: an AST count of Lever(...) calls carrying domain= in src/capacity/levers.py returns 0. findings.detail: Appended in D16/D17's shape, after D17, with the same '---' separator.
